subject: Workplace Skills
title: Handling Credit Theft
description: A 60-second lesson on Handling Credit Theft.

hook.text: He proposed the idea in a one-on-one. His peer presented it at the leadership meeting as their own.

buildup.text: Credit theft is common but rarely intentional. People genuinely forget where ideas originated.

discovery.text: Prevent it by documenting ideas in writing first: a Slack message, an email, a shared doc with a timestamp.

twist.text: Confronting publicly embarrasses everyone. A private 'I noticed my idea came up' preserves the relationship.

climax.text: If it's repeated, escalate calmly with evidence. Patterns deserve a conversation with your manager.

punchline.text: Write it down first. Timestamps don't lie.

quiz.question: What's the best way to prevent credit theft for your ideas?
options: Never share ideas until they're fully developed
Document them in writing with timestamps before sharing
Announce ideas loudly in front of witnesses
